slots_and_copies.name: trailer_flag_block
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Not a mirrored copy; single shared 8-byte block immediately after the three slots (EEPROM block index 288). Observed 0xFF..FF (cap-00) -> 0x00..00 (cap-01); semantics (flag vs counter) unresolved.

magic_signatures.ascii: AMREBMOB\xd2\x002XAM-N (raw); reversing each 8-byte half yields 'BOMBERMA' + 'N-MAX2\x00\xd2' -> 'BOMBERMAN-MAX2' + 2 trailing bytes

checksums.name: unidentified_candidate
checksums.formula_detail: No checksum/CRC routine was found among the 87 decompiled functions. Both .sav samples are byte-identical across the entire 0x000-0x8FF record region, so no checksum formula could be exercised against changing data; only the independent 0x900-0x907 trailer block differed, ruling it out as a content-dependent checksum of the preceding data (it flips unconditionally, not as a function of unchanged data).

io_driver_functions.notes: Raw DMA3 transfer primitive: programs SAD/DAD/CNT (CNT |= 0x80000000 enable bit), busy-waits completion bit 0x8000. Address-agnostic; both callers pass literal 0xD000000 (GBA EEPROM I/O port).
DMA/IRQ-channel enable helper bracketing the write path in FUN_0806bb40; sets an IRQ-enable-shaped bit pattern and stages a second source/length pair.
Paired teardown helper for 0x0806b960; clears the bit pattern it set.

EEPROM block READ: validates block_index against a runtime block-count limit, issues a read-request bitstream then a 68-halfword (4 dummy + 64 data bits) response transfer via FUN_0806ba08, both targeting 0xD000000. Matches the standard GBA EEPROM serial read protocol exactly (length = addr_bits + 3 for the request, 0x44=68 for the response).

EEPROM block WRITE: validates block_index, serializes 8 input bytes + address bits + '10' write opcode + stop bit, issues via FUN_0806ba08 with length = addr_bits + 67 (2 opcode + 64 data + 1 stop), matching the standard protocol exactly. No caller found in the 87-function corpus -- top-level entry point, trigger chain unresolved.

WRITE-VERIFY: calls FUN_0806ba88 to read back a block and compares it word-by-word against an expected 8-byte buffer, returning 0x8000 on mismatch. No caller found in the 87-function corpus -- top-level entry point, trigger chain unresolved.

fields.name: slot_magic_header
fields.update_mechanism: unknown - no writer present in the 87-function corpus; value is identical across all 3 slots and both samples
fields.evidence: Direct byte read of saves/*.sav at offsets 0x000, 0x300, 0x600; reversing each 8-byte half yields legible ASCII 'BOMBERMA'+'N-MAX2\x00\xd2' matching the release title text from this packet's own metadata.

fields.name: slot_reserved_padding
fields.evidence: Direct byte read; zero-filled run identical in all 3 slots and both samples.

fields.name: slot_flag_array
fields.evidence: Python Counter over in-slot bytes 0x30-0x11F (120 u16 entries) shows only two distinct values (0 and 1) in both samples, consistent with a boolean/flag array; no writer/reader traced and no semantic labels assigned per clean-room rule.

fields.name: slot_record_table_main
fields.evidence: Hex inspection of in-slot bytes 0x120-0x2BF shows a 16-byte-period repeating row shape across 26 rows, with only 4 of each row's 8 u16 words ever non-zero; identical across all 3 slots and both samples. No semantic meaning assigned.

fields.name: slot_record_table_summary
fields.evidence: Same 16-byte row shape as slot_record_table_main but larger-magnitude values and only 4 rows; distinguished purely by position/magnitude, not by any traced code. Possible aggregate/summary rows -- unverified.

fields.name: trailer_flag_block
fields.update_mechanism: unknown - sole byte difference between the two sample .sav files; the entire 2304-byte redundant-slot region is otherwise byte-identical between samples
fields.evidence: Byte diff of saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt and independent Python re-diff; absolute offset 0x900 equals EEPROM block index 288, immediately after the 3x768-byte slot region (96 blocks each).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Reset trailer_flag_block from 0x00..00 back to 0xff..ff (its cap-00 value) while leaving all 3 slots untouched.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this block is a pure one-shot 'ever saved' flag, load behavior should be unaffected (data still present in all 3 slots). If it gates whether the save is considered valid at all, the game should treat the cartridge as blank/new-game.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: In slot 0 only (in-slot offset 0x30), flip one u16 flag-array entry (0x0001 -> 0x0000), leaving slot 1/2 copies at offsets 0x330/0x630 unchanged.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If a majority-vote/repair reader exists across the 3 redundant slots, slot 0 should be silently corrected back to match slots 1/2 on next read or save. If no such reader exists, the single-slot divergence should persist, disproving the redundancy-repair hypothesis.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero out in-slot offset 0x00-0x07 (first half of the magic header) in slot 0 only.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Tests whether a per-slot identity/validity check exists; a validity check would cause the game to ignore/rebuild slot 0 from slot 1 or 2, while no check would leave slot 0 silently corrupted.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Toggle one flag-array entry (in-slot offset 0x31, byte 0x01 -> 0x00) identically across all 3 slots (0x31/0x331/0x631) to avoid confounding with the single-slot divergence test.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Unknown pending event-aligned capture; establishes only whether this array is consumed at all during boot/load.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Raise one non-zero word in the slot_record_table_main row at in-slot offset 0x120 (word index 2, in-slot byte 0x133) by +0x10, identically across all 3 slots.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Unknown; establishes read/consumption of this table as a prerequisite before any future semantic labeling.

open_questions: No checksum/CRC routine was found in the 87-function corpus; because both .sav samples share byte-identical primary data, checksum presence/absence over the record region is unproven, not disproven.

Callers of the EEPROM WRITE (0x0806bb40) and WRITE-VERIFY (0x0806bc24) entry points are absent from the supplied corpus (callgraph.json lists callers: [] for both); the full gameplay-to-flush trigger chain is unknown.
No slot-comparison/selection/repair function was found; the apparent triple-redundant mirrored-slot layout's actual read-side selection rule is unverified.

Semantic meaning of the 120-entry flag array (in-slot 0x30-0x11F) and the two numeric record tables (in-slot 0x120-0x2FF) is unknown; only structural shape could be derived without importing outside game-specific research.

Whether the trailer block at absolute offset 0x900 is a one-shot flag or the low bits of an incrementing counter cannot be determined from only two samples (0xFF..FF -> 0x00..00); a third capture after additional save-triggering gameplay would disambiguate.

Exact EEPROM address bit-width (6-bit for 512B vs 14-bit for 8K EEPROM) is loaded from a runtime table in FUN_0806ba88/FUN_0806bb40 rather than a compile-time literal, so it could not be read directly from the decompilation; inferred as 14-bit from the 8192-byte .sav size per generic GBA hardware behavior.
Meaning of the two non-ASCII trailing bytes in the magic header (stored 0xD2, 0x00) is unresolved -- possibly a version/region tag.
